policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'draught-house' (privy) renders the sense shared by both readings: the ketiv מחראות is the plain word for latrines, and the qere מוצאות is the conventional euphemism for the same place. The English chooses neither the literal nor the euphemistic term distinctively, and no textual note is mapped to this unit; the base qere fallback carries the projection.
